reviewer: Codex native-size visual review, reconciled with Grok 4.5 high-effort correction audit

questions.question: Is the protagonist identifiable without a label?
questions.reason: The swept hair, teal torso, dark outline, and diagonal strap separate the protagonist from nearby residents at native 1x.

questions.question: Is the nearest open doorway distinguishable from a closed wall?
questions.reason: The open cell has a pale opening and dark threshold. The adjacent wall keeps its stucco face, terracotta band, and dark core.

questions.question: Are solid objects distinguishable from low-contrast ground detail?
questions.reason: Furniture, signs, lamps, planters, and palms use dark contact edges and compact silhouettes. Sand ripples and shells stay thin and low contrast.

questions.question: Are the protagonist, Linda, and generic resident distinguishable by shape, not only color?
questions.reason: The protagonist has swept hair and a strap. Linda has long side hair and earrings. The resident has a high quiff and wide glasses.

questions.question: Does the ground avoid a dominant one-cell stamp or grid?
questions.reason: Four sand and floor variants remove repeated 2x2 blocks. The fixed sand board has no identical diagonal run longer than four cells.

questions.question: Are floor, wall, roof, prop, and character layers separable in grayscale?
questions.reason: The grayscale frame keeps dark walls and roofs, mid-value props and characters, and light exterior sand as separate value groups.
